html:
SMTO-EXE-0164 — SMTO had no place to save this document

GUID: 9d6c4692-f08e-5e87-8b90-b188101e6a01
Slug: office-artifact-failure
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • SMTO normally saves edited documents as a new file inside the conversation, but this request didn't come with a conversation it could save into. The original document wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make the request from a conversation in SMTO, not from a separate tool or automation. Edited documents are saved as new files that belong to the conversation that asked for them.
  2. If you want the file somewhere specific, tell SMTO the full folder and a new file name on the Gateway computer, with the same ending as the document (.docx, .xlsx or .pptx). With an exact new location, SMTO doesn't need the conversation's storage area, but it won't replace a file that already exists.
  3. If the document came from another conversation, attach it again with Add context in this conversation. SMTO can only reuse saved files from the same conversation that created them.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the new document and it appears in the conversation or in the folder you named.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Your original document is never overwritten by SMTO, so there's nothing to restore.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Office operation could not resolve a run artifact workspace: an artifact-workspace:// path arrived without a scoped artifact root, or a mutation without output_path lacked the conversation_id/run_id needed to create the run's artifact destination (office.artifact_failure).

What this means

  • An artifact-workspace path lacked its scoped root, or implicit output publication lacked the owning run/conversation needed to create an artifact destination. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • An artifact-workspace path lacked its scoped root, or implicit output publication lacked the owning run/conversation needed to create an artifact destination.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect artifact-workspace scope and run/conversation identity, distinguishing input artifact resolution from output publication.

How to fix it

  • Run the Office operation inside a native conversation run so the runtime supplies _artifact_scope (conversation_id and run_id) to the Gateway, or pass an explicit new output_path under File policy whose parent exists. artifact-workspace:// sources resolve only inside the same conversation/run's workspace.
  • Run in a conversation/run with artifact collection, or supply an exact new output_path under File policy.

Retry and execution caution

  • Run in a conversation/run with artifact collection, or supply an exact new output_path under File policy.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended artifact resolves in its owning workspace or a new authorized output_path is supplied.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
